sources.title: ITAA 1997 s 26-50, expenses for a leisure facility
sources.fact: Read 15 October 2026 in the ATO legal database. Section 26-50(1) denies deductions relating to a leisure facility, defined in s 26-50(2) as land or a building used or held for use for holidays or recreation. Section 26-50(3)(b)(ii) excepts a facility used or held at all times in the income year mainly to produce assessable income in the nature of rents and similar charges; s 26-50(4) allows a reasonable part where that use covers part of the year; s 26-50(7) is an anti-avoidance rule.
sources.limitations: ATO legal database reproduction. Open the compilation in force for the income year.

sources.title: TR 2026/1 Income tax: rental property income and deductions for individuals who are not in business
sources.fact: Read 15 October 2026. Issued 20 May 2026; applies to income years before and after issue, subject to Appendix 2. Paragraph 138 states the Commissioner will not devote compliance resources to reviewing whether s 26-50 applies to expenses for holiday homes that are rental properties incurred before 1 July 2026. Paragraph 6 states renting out a property, including on an online sharing platform, does not of itself mean carrying on a business.
sources.limitations: Public ruling; the PDF is the authorised version. Confirm current status and any addendum.

sources.title: PCG 2026/2 Apportionment of rental property deductions - ATO compliance approach
sources.fact: Read 15 October 2026. Issued 20 May 2026. Sets out apportionment methodologies for rental property deductions consistent with TR 2026/1.
sources.limitations: Compliance guideline, not law. Confirm the method suits the facts and the current status.

sources.title: PCG 2026/3 Application of section 26-50 of the ITAA 1997 to holiday homes that you also rent out - ATO compliance approach
sources.fact: Read 15 October 2026. Issued 20 May 2026. Uses green, amber and red risk zones for s 26-50. Green indicators include high income-producing occupancy in peak holiday periods and limited personal use; red includes blocking out peak periods each year for personal use. Paragraphs 12 and 13 apply the TR 2026/1 paragraph 138 approach to expenses incurred before 1 July 2026.
sources.limitations: Compliance guideline, not law. A zone is a risk rating, not a decision on s 26-50.

sources.title: ITAA 1997 s 26-31, travel related to use of residential premises as residential accommodation
sources.fact: Read 15 October 2026. Section 26-31(1) denies travel-related losses or outgoings incurred in gaining assessable income from residential premises used as residential accommodation unless necessarily incurred in carrying on a business; s 26-31(2) excepts listed entity types.
sources.limitations: ATO legal database reproduction. Open the compilation in force for the income year.

sources.title: ITAA 1997 s 40-27, second-hand assets in residential property
sources.fact: Read 15 October 2026. Section 40-27 further reduces decline in value deductions for second-hand depreciating assets used in residential premises to provide residential accommodation, subject to its exceptions.
sources.limitations: ATO legal database reproduction. Read the conditions and exceptions for the period.

sources.title: GST Act s 40-35, residential rent
sources.fact: Read 15 October 2026. A lease, hire or licence of residential premises is input taxed, other than a supply of commercial residential premises or accommodation in them provided by the owner or controller (s 40-35(1)(a)), and only to the extent the premises are to be used predominantly for residential accommodation, regardless of the term of occupation (s 40-35(2)(a)).
sources.limitations: ATO legal database reproduction. Read with the s 195-1 definitions and Division 87.

sources.title: GST Act s 195-1, dictionary
sources.fact: Read 15 October 2026. Residential premises means land or a building occupied, or intended and capable of being occupied, as a residence or for residential accommodation, regardless of the term of occupation. Commercial residential premises includes a hotel, motel, inn, hostel or boarding house, a caravan park or camping ground, and anything similar to residential premises described in those paragraphs.
sources.limitations: Long dictionary page; only the two definitions were read.

sources.title: GST Act s 11-15, creditable purpose
sources.fact: Read 15 October 2026. Under s 11-15(2)(a) an acquisition is not for a creditable purpose to the extent it relates to making supplies that would be input taxed.
sources.limitations: ATO legal database reproduction. Check the exceptions in the section for the facts.

sources.title: GST Act s 188-15, current GST turnover
sources.fact: Read 15 October 2026. Current GST turnover excludes input taxed supplies (s 188-15(1)(a)), supplies not for consideration and supplies not made in connection with an enterprise carried on.
sources.limitations: Projected GST turnover (s 188-20) was not read.

sources.title: GST Act s 23-5, who is required to be registered
sources.fact: Read 15 October 2026. Registration is required if the entity is carrying on an enterprise and its GST turnover meets the registration turnover threshold.
sources.limitations: The threshold amount is set elsewhere and was not recorded.

sources.title: GSTR 2012/6 Goods and services tax: commercial residential premises
sources.fact: Read 15 October 2026. The ruling sets out the Commissioner's view on commercial residential premises. The page states an updated version was issued as a draft for public comment until 19 December 2025.
sources.limitations: Check whether the draft update has been finalised before relying on any paragraph.

sources.title: ATO: What is the SERR?
sources.fact: Read 15 October 2026 (page last updated 20 January 2026). The Sharing Economy Reporting Regime is established under Subdivision 396-B of Schedule 1 to the Taxation Administration Act 1953. Electronic distribution platform operators report twice a year, by 31 January and 31 July. Reporting commenced on 1 July 2023 for taxi travel, including ride-sourcing, and short-term accommodation.
sources.limitations: ATO web guidance. The reporting obligation is the platform operator's, not the host's.

sources.title: SRO Victoria: Short stay levy
sources.fact: Read 15 October 2026. The short stay levy is charged on the total booking fee for a stay in short-stay accommodation in Victoria, is collected by booking platforms or hosts, and applies to short stays in Victorian properties from 1 January 2025 under the Short Stay Levy Act 2024.
sources.limitations: Landing page only. Read the Act and SRO guidance for the rate, exclusions and registration.

sources.title: ITAA 1997 s 118-190, use of dwelling for producing assessable income
sources.fact: Read 15 October 2026. Section 118-190(1) gives only a partial main residence exemption where the dwelling was used to produce assessable income during the period and interest on money borrowed to acquire it could have been deducted.
sources.limitations: Read with s 118-192 and the absence rules before any calculation.
